ahead: SCALE_TRANSITION.md gives a precise negative result: the dyadic scale-transition on CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's Energy(N)=E_corr(N) identity fails, and fails specifically at scale k=0 (and throughout the provable range k<=(1/4)log_2 N), not at some vague general obstruction. Two mechanisms were tried and both fail: (a) a global block recursion using the classical Vinogradov-Korobov PNT rate applied per dyadic block, which produces a bound on Delta_k(N) that is strictly worse than the trivial N^3 order throughout its entire provable range (the naive per-block-times-block-count blowup); (b) a local empirical geometric-decay recursion (Delta_k/Delta_{k-1} approx 1/2, measured directly from the existing results_s8_candidate_energy.json), which cannot close because any such recursion bottoms out at Delta_0(N), a quantity already identified in CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md as exactly as hard as E_corr(N) itself. No theta beyond the already-established kappa<1/10 (CORRECTED_RH_BRIDGE.md eq 21) or the separately proposed theta=1/10 (ENDPOINT_BOUND.md) is produced; this document does not reprove or weaken either. The one open door named in Section 4/7: an aggregate (large-sieve-style) second-moment estimate for block-sum discrepancies across many shift-blocks simultaneously, rather than a block-by-block worst-case bound, is not ruled out in principle -- only shown absent from the currently inherited toolkit, and shown to reduce to the same long-window gap LOCALIZED_MIXED_ENERGY.md already left open (its eq 20).

work.what: Investigate whether an unconditional large-sieve-type (aggregate) second-moment estimate exists or can be proved for the quantity sum over shift-blocks B of length s of |sum_{h in B}(r_N(h)-C_N(h))|^2, for short block lengths s (e.g. s = O(1) up to s = N^{1/4}), that beats the naive block-by-block bound of O(N^5 e^{-2c L(N)}/s^2) obtained by squaring the classical PNT-rate discrepancy bound per block and summing over the N/s blocks independently (L(N) = (log N)^{3/5}(log log N)^{-1/5}, the Vinogradov-Korobov rate already used in LOCALIZED_MIXED_ENERGY.md eq 18-19). This is exactly the input SCALE_TRANSITION.md (hunts/prime_pair_error/SCALE_TRANSITION.md) Section 4 identifies as missing and needed to make the scale-transition approach to CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's dyadic energy decomposition (hunts/prime_pair_error/CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md) work at fine scales, where CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's own measured tables (results_s8_candidate_energy.json) show close to half of E_corr(N) is concentrated. Read SCALE_TRANSITION.md Sections 3-4 in full for the precise definitions (x_h = r_N(h)-C_N(h), the block-sum discrepancy Lemma and its proof, the granted-assumption caveat) before starting. A precise negative result (e.g. showing no unconditional such aggregate estimate can beat the block-by-block bound at short lengths without new input, or identifying exactly what new arithmetic fact would be needed) is a valid, complete outcome, just as a positive construction would be.
